originalLive.Presentation: {patientName}, a 39-year-old woman, visits the clinic with an enlarging extremity mass. Ultrasound places its superficial margin beneath the investing fascia, but cannot show the deep margin.

keyOrderNotice: Key shown first for review only. Runtime answer choices are randomized.

before.label: Image-guided core biopsy with an anterior approach through rectus femoris
before.rationale: Obtains diagnostic cores from viable tissue while keeping the planned tract within the tumor-bearing compartment.

before.label: Image-guided core biopsy with a medial approach through adductor muscle
before.rationale: Selects the shorter route to the more intensely enhancing region but contaminates a separate muscle compartment.

before.label: Open incisional biopsy with an anterior approach through rectus femoris
before.rationale: Uses the better tract but escalates to an open procedure before a feasible initial core approach has been attempted.

before.label: Open incisional biopsy with a medial approach through adductor muscle
before.rationale: Combines premature open sampling with the path that traverses a separate muscle compartment.

after.label: Image-guided core biopsy with an anterior approach through rectus femoris
after.rationale: Both targets enhance. An anterior core biopsy follows the proposed resection exposure: its skin entry and intramuscular tract lie within the proposed specimen. It also avoids crossing the separate medial compartment.

after.label: Image-guided core biopsy with a medial approach through adductor longus
after.rationale: The shorter medial route reaches more intensely enhancing tissue, but crosses adductor longus outside the proposed specimen. That tract would not be removed with the currently planned specimen.

after.label: Open incisional biopsy with an anterior approach through rectus femoris
after.rationale: The anterior skin entry and intramuscular tract are inside the proposed specimen, but an initial image-guided core is preferred when percutaneous sampling is feasible. Open incisional biopsy is a selected alternative, not the initial choice on these findings.

after.label: Open incisional biopsy with a medial approach through adductor longus
after.rationale: This combines an open initial procedure despite feasible core access with a medial tract through adductor longus outside the proposed specimen.

explanation: Choose image-guided core sampling through the anterior approach. Both targets enhance; the stronger enhancement and shorter medial route do not outweigh tract planning. The biopsy tract, including its skin entry, must be removable with the definitive specimen. The stated anterior resection includes that tract; staying in the tumor-bearing compartment by itself would not establish this. Feasible core sampling is the preferred initial method; selected cases may require open biopsy.
inference: Interpret enhancing solid targets and the documented resection field, then combine tract removability with the preferred feasible initial biopsy method.
focus: Initial core method plus tract removability under an explicitly documented resection plan
whatChanged: Restore percutaneous access for both targets; state the proposed exposure and specimen relationship; explain removal of the entire tract with the specimen. clinicalReviewBoundary: Melissa Rowland and musculoskeletal radiology/sarcoma review must confirm the constructed access, specimen outline, skin entry and entire tract geometry. No clinician confirmation has occurred. General source guidance does not certify a safe operative trajectory.
